newsitem.title: UK: UK air security comprehensive without slowing trade.
newsitem.headline: UK air security comprehensive without slowing trade.

text.p: The British air cargo security regime is designed to ensure that all cargo on international flights is subject to appropriate checks before loading, Kenneth Robinson, head of the Airlines and Cargo Branch of the UK Department of Transport Transport and Security Division (TRANSEC) said.
But the DOT was very aware when considering security measures that they must be simple, effective and not a barrier to trade, Robinson added.
Controls such x-rays, hand-searching or full flight simulation can be carried out at registered cargo agents or airlines, he told the SMi's Competitiveness and Profitability in Air Cargo Conference.

The UK system also includes a fast-track system where cargo from a known shipper passing through a listed agent can bypass normal security requirements. This option is only available in a low threat security situation.
As some 80 percent of aircargo is carried in the bellyhold of passenger aircraft, it is essential that it has equally tough security measures as for passenger baggage.

TRANSEC keeps a record of all terrorist linked "incidents" involving civil aviation around the world and came up with a total of over 1,200 between 1970 and 1995 or about one a week, Robinson noted. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
